Shane, how do you, I guess, go forward with Mooney?
Like, do you monitor that, how he's feeling, and then go from there?
Yeah, he had a good day at work today, and then we'll see how he feels tomorrow.
But I think he's in a good place right now.
How does C .J.
Allen look this week, and is there, I mean, how do you evaluate him going forward?
Is there a chance he can play more this week?
Yeah, absolutely.
He had a good week at work, and so, you know, we take that always into consideration, look at the week of preparation.
But he had a good week of work, and we'll see where it goes on Sunday.
Was there enough last week that wasn't allowed plenty of time, but was there enough to make some determinations?
Yeah, what did he have, six plays last week?
But he did some good things in those six plays.
Like I said, we got some good practice in this week with him, and we'll go from there.
What kind of a week did Slayton have?
He did good.
He did some good things for us.
So we'll see how much volume this week and go from there.
The fact that you're asking to do kind of a primary thing, getting deep maybe, Does that make it easier to get him in quicker?
Yeah, a little bit.
I think still, too.
I mean, it's been three weeks since he's played football, so it's still getting him acclimated, you know, to our offense and all those different things.
So he's in shape.
That part made it easier, I imagine.
Yeah, like I said, he's in shape, but he's still got to get back into football.
It's been three weeks, like I said, so, yeah.
Shane, do you believe in must -wins in September?
I believe that all wins are important.
I think every game's important.
I think this game obviously is big because it's a division game.
I think it carries a little more weight, especially in the division.
But you've got to be good every weekend and week out, but you've really got to be great November, December football.
But, you know, you've got to win every game.
You know, you go out and play.
We know Nico Collins obviously has had a lot of success against the Colts, but status is up in the air.
What other areas do you look at in their offensive sale?
Okay, this will have to be our keys.
Yeah, I think the tight end, like I mentioned on Wednesday, he had a ton of targets last week.
They've been targeting him.
He's a really good football player, so got to do a great job with him.
You know, the running back Montgomery, like I said, is a really good football player as well.
So we've got to do a great job of tackling, taking those guys away, and then obviously the other wideouts that they have that are going to step up and replace Iniko.
When a guy has a big game like Kelsey did and then the next team has a tight end who's caught a lot, do you just kind of assume that's going to be part of the game plan for them?
It depends.
You know, obviously they're watching the tape, so see what they have planned up for us early in the game and be ready to go.
What's that balance of like their ends can wreck a game, but you also need to run your offense and then can't?
Yeah, I think first and foremost, I mean, that is the biggest thing.
These two are the best in the business without a doubt.
So we've got to do a great job handling those guys, because if we don't handle those guys, it's going to be hard to get the offense going.
But we've got to do a great job with those two guys on the edges.
And then we go from there.
Do you have any opinion on Matt Gonzalez?
Fine.
You know, I think he was drinking a Coca -Cola.
I think.
But obviously you've got to respect the league's decisions on those things.
